summary: Franz-Karl Ehrhard works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1976–1998) under Lambert Schmithausen (~1980–1987). He served at the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993) and was a professor at the University of Munich (2003–2019).
François Gros was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lyon (~1952–1956). He held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1977–2002).
François Jacob studied at the University of Paris (~1938–1947) and Sorbonne University (~1950–1954). He held posts at the Pasteur Institute (1960) and the Collège de France (1964).

Françoise Pommaret works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at INALCO (~1976–1979), Sorbonne University, and the University of Paris. Her career includes posts at CNRS (from ~1989), INALCO, and the Royal University of Bhutan (~2008).
Françoise Robin specializes in Tibetology. She studied at INALCO (~1998–1999) under Heather Stoddard (~1999–2003). She held posts at the Collège de France (2009–2015) and INALCO (2011, 2013–2014).

Fred Pfeil worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned degrees at Amherst College (~1967–1971) and Stanford University (~1971–1973). He taught at Stanford, Stephens College, Oregon State University, and Trinity College, Hartford (~1985–2005).
Freda Bedi worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at St Hugh's College, Oxford (~1929–1933) and under Mahasi Sayadaw (~1953).

Frederick James Furnivall was a linguist who studied at University College London (~1841–1842) and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1842–1847). He served as Secretary of the Philological Society (1853–1910) and taught at the Working Men's College (~1854–1910).
Frederick M. Asher was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota as a professor (~1971–2021).
Frederick M. Smith specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Ludo Rocher and held positions as professor and professor emeritus at the University of Iowa (attested 2006–2026).

Frederick William Thomas was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He served at the India Office Library (1898–1927) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937).

Frederik David Kan Bosch studied Indology and history/archaeology under Jacob Samuel Speyer and Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck (~1910–1914). He served in the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (~1916–1936) and held professorships at Utrecht (1938–1945) and Leiden (1946–1957).

Fredrik Barth studied at the University of Chicago (1946–1949) and Cambridge under Edmund Ronald Leach (~1953–1957). He was a professor at the University of Bergen (1961–1972) and Oslo (1974), and taught at Emory, Harvard, and Boston University (~1997–2008).

Friederike Assandri works in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Heidelberg University under Rudolf G. Wagner, Günther Debon, and Günther-Dietz Sontheimer, and later held a post there (attested 2013).

Friedhelm Hardy worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at the University of Cologne and the University of Oxford (1967). He served as Wilde Lecturer at Oxford (1985–1987) and Professor of Indian Religions at King's College London (~1990–2004).

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff, an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Sinologist, earned doctorates at the University of Paris under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He was a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1964–1982), Hamburg (1982–1993), and Vienna (~1982–2009).

Friedrich August Rosen was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp in 1824. He was appointed Professor of Oriental Languages at University College London (1828–1831) and Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1834).
Friedrich August Ukert was a history and archaeology scholar who completed studies at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1800–1801) and the University of Jena (~1801–1803).

Friedrich August Wolf was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen (~1777–1779) and held a post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1783–1807).

Friedrich Bechtel was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Theodor Benfey and August Fick at the University of Göttingen (~1873–1876). He served as Dozent at Göttingen (1884) and full professor at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1895).
